statement.text:
The function dn (σ, τ ) = (1/n)·|{x ∈ {1, . . . , n} | σ(x) ̸= τ (x)}| is a distance on
the symmetric group Sn . For a finitely generated group G, an almost-homomorphism
is a sequence of set-theoretic maps fn : G → Sn satisfying dn (fn (g)fn (h), fn (gh)) → 0
as n → ∞ for all g, h ∈ G. An almost-homomorphism {fn } is said to be close to a
homomorphism if there is a sequence of group homomorphisms ρn : G → Sn such that
dn (ρn (g), fn (g)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g ∈ G. The group G is said to be permutation
stable if every almost-homomorphism of G is close to a homomorphism.
    Conjecture: Metabelian groups are permutation-stable.                        A. Lubotzky
